$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs one suite locally with
exactly the same steps, so the two cannot drift.
Every suite states what is compared and, where anything is canonicalized away, why. That
`why` used to live in a YAML comment next to a copy of the comparator; it is the part that
must not be lost, because canonicalization is how a bit-identity claim quietly weakens.
`status` is either `oracle-backed` (the golden is regenerated by the oracle in CI and
compared, which is the bar) or `unchecked` (the golden is committed and read by the Rust
tests, but no CI step has ever regenerated it against the oracle). See
docs/decisions/0008 for what the unchecked goldens turned out to be.

ci.$why: Suites are grouped into jobs of this size. One job per suite would restore the ~1 GB oracle image once per suite, which costs more runner time than it buys; one job for everything is what the hand-written workflow did, and it hid every suite after the first failure.

$why: The covering-array job used to name its tools in four places in ci.template.yml: the
`cargo build --bin` line, one `run_array.py` invocation, one `--log` on measure.py, and
one path in the dirty check. Four lists that had to agree, edited by hand, in the job
whose whole purpose is to say how much of a tool's argument surface the port reproduces.
Declaring the tool once and generating the job is what makes the fan-out to the other
hundred-odd ported tools a one-line change per tool instead of a four-place edit.
`status` carries the same distinction the suites' does. `measured` means the number in
tools/coverage/measured.json was produced by this job on real x86-64 and is re-derived on
every run, so a port that grows or loses argument surface fails here. `pending` means the
array runs and the run publishes the measurement as an artefact, but nothing is committed
yet: a coverage number produced on a developer machine is the same mistake as a golden
produced there (decision 0008), and an emulated container is not the pinned platform.
Committing the published artefact and flipping the status to `measured` is the deliberate
act that turns the run into a claim.

suites.title: the header MergeBamAlignment builds from three files
suites.why: The records are measured by `mergebamalignment`; this is the header they arrive under, and it is built from three files rather than one: the sequences from the reference dictionary, the read groups from the UNMAPPED bam, the programs from the ALIGNED one. The temp directory is canonicalised to `<dir>`, because the `UR` and the tool's own command line both carry it; what is compared is which lines are there and what they hold.

cases.why: Twelve runs: the whole header; the reference named the long way round, through a directory and back out of it, which says whether the UR is canonicalised; a read group the aligner rewrote and an unmapped bam with none; a chain of two programs; two aligned files whose program ids collide; a whole program record from the command line and half of one, which is refused; comments in both inputs; queryname and unsorted output; and two aligned headers that disagree with the dictionary, by length and by name.

suites.title: what MergeBamAlignment does to a pair
suites.why: A pair is not two records merged twice: the mate fields of each end are written from the other end's alignment, the insert size is computed from both, the proper-pair flag is decided by the merger rather than copied from the aligner, and overlapping ends are clipped so the same base is not counted twice. Several data-line rows share one (kind, case) key, so the full line sequence is compared.

cases.why: Eleven runs: the mate fields the aligner wrote, which are wrong on purpose, replaced by the ones the other end implies; the same pair with the ends swapped, which signs the insert size; a pair the aligner called proper across two contigs, with and without ALIGNER_PROPER_PAIR_FLAGS; a run without ADD_MATE_CIGAR; overlapping ends soft-clipped, unclipped and hard-clipped; one end with no alignment; a soft-clipped end, which says what the insert size is measured between; and the deprecated PAIRED_RUN.

suites.title: what MergeBamAlignment clips, and what it unmaps
suites.why: Three things shorten or remove an alignment on the way through: the contig it runs off the end of, the adapter the unmapped bam marked in it, and the contamination filter that decides an alignment is too short to believe. Several data-line rows share one (kind, case) key, so the full line sequence is compared.

cases.why: Eleven runs: an alignment ten bases off the end of its contig, the same one already ending in a soft clip, and one that fits; an adapter marked by XT, clipped and left alone; a short alignment kept, unmapped as a contaminant, and kept again under a lower MIN_UNCLIPPED_BASES; the same shortness clipped at one end only, which is not a contaminant at all; and the three unmapped-read strategies over the same contaminant.

suites.title: which alignment MergeBamAlignment calls primary
suites.why: An aligner may report a read several times, and the merger has to choose which of those alignments is primary, mark the rest as secondary, and decide whether to carry them at all. Four strategies make that choice and they do not agree. Several data-line rows share one (kind, case) key, so the full line sequence is compared.

cases.why: Ten runs: three alignments of one read under each of the four strategies and with the secondaries dropped; the same three with the aligner naming one primary, under two strategies; and a pair with two alignments each under the default, under MostDistant, and under the strategy that will not read a pair at all.

suites.title: CollectJumpingLibraryMetrics
CompareMetrics
SortGff
CheckDuplicateMarking

cases.why: Fifteen cases: every name agreeing, one disagreement, two on one name, a name appearing once, a coordinate-sorted file, a secondary and a supplementary disagreement under ALL and under PRIMARY_ONLY, an unmapped one under PRIMARY_ONLY and PRIMARY_MAPPED_ONLY, an improper pair under PRIMARY_MAPPED_ONLY and PRIMARY_PROPER_PAIR_ONLY, a secondary record the sort puts last, and a run with no output file.

suites.why: The comparison is against the FIRST record of each name and not against the record before it, so a name whose flags go true, false, false reports two bad records and writes its name twice. The mode's skip happens BEFORE the tally, so a skipped record is neither compared nor remembered and the same file is clean under PRIMARY_ONLY and bad under ALL.

suites.title: CollectQualityYieldMetricsFlow

cases.why: Thirteen cases: one read, homopolymers beside singles, two quality levels, a quality between the two thresholds, a vendor-failed read, secondary and supplementary reads in and out, one included while the other is not, the histogram, a read with no flow matrix, and an empty file.

suites.why: A skipped secondary or supplementary read is counted NOWHERE, TOTAL_READS included, which is not what happens to a vendor-failed one: that is counted in TOTAL_READS and left out of PF_READS. PF_Q20_EQUIVALENT_YIELD is the SUM of the flow qualities divided by twenty, so four flows at quality 40 yield 8 and eight flows at quality 25 yield 10. And PF_Q20_FLOWS counts every flow at 20 or over, the 30s included, so it is never smaller than PF_Q30_FLOWS.

suites.title: the map from VCF path to sample name, and the order its lines come out in
suites.why: The line is the PATH first and the name second, which is the opposite way round from the tool's name. The lines come out of a HashMap keyed by the path STRING, so the order is neither the arguments' nor sorted, the same file named once plainly and once with a dot in the middle is two lines, and the same string twice is one.

cases.why: Eleven cases: one input, three inputs and the same three reversed, the same path twice, one path with a dot in it, two paths naming the same sample, no sample, two samples, a file that is not a VCF, a good input before a bad one, and an input that is not there.

suites.title: the haplotype database read against the reference, which is what decides REF
suites.why: REF is the allele that DISAGREES with the reference. The code asks which allele matches the reference base and then writes THAT one as ALT, so a row whose major allele is the reference base and a row whose minor allele is come out with the same REF and ALT and only the frequency tells them apart. The phase set is the position of the block's FIRST SNP and not of the row named as the anchor.

cases.why: Nine cases: a row whose major allele is the reference base and one whose minor allele is, a phased block of three whose anchor is named second, three rows out of order over two contigs, a row neither of whose alleles matches, a table with no header, a short row, an anchor naming no row, and a table with no rows at all.

suites.title: a haplotype database moved onto another reference, and what is rewritten on the way
suites.why: The exit code for a failed liftover is 101 and not 1, and the file is still written: a database whose every SNP fails leaves a file holding its header and its column line alone. The alleles are never complemented across a negative-strand chain, so chr2:50 A/C becomes chrB:851 A/C, and the anchor column is rewritten rather than carried.

cases.why: Eight cases: a block that lifts whole, one SNP past the end of the chain, a whole block that fails, a negative-strand chain, a block spanning two contigs, a dictionary missing a contig the chain lifts to, a contig the chain does not cover, and a database whose every SNP fails.

suites.title: which reads a positional mask keeps, which has no randomness in it at all
suites.why: There is no randomness in the selection at all: the same file downsampled twice keeps exactly the same reads. What decides is the tile's own extent, taken from the reads themselves and then widened by its span over the read count, so the same coordinates are kept on one tile and dropped on another. A fraction over a half does not grow the circle: it builds one for 1-FRACTION and keeps the reads INSIDE it.

cases.why: Sixteen cases: five fractions, the same run twice, two tiles of different extents, the duplicate flag cleared and kept, STOP_AFTER, an unparseable read name, two fractions out of range, and a second run refused and then allowed.

suites.title: the marks a duplicate-marked file already carries, tallied
suites.why: There is one row per library NAMED IN THE HEADER whether a read ever used it or not, so a file with no reads at all still writes a row of zeros. The halving of the paired counts is an integer division, so a lone paired read reports no pairs examined. And an estimated library size of zero makes every histogram bin NaN, which the writer renders as `?`.

cases.why: Eleven cases: two pairs with one duplicate, an odd number of paired reads, an unpaired pair, a half-mapped pair, an unmapped duplicate, a secondary and a supplementary duplicate, two libraries, a read group with no library, every pair a duplicate, only unmapped reads, and a file with no reads.

suites.title: what the three regexes accept, and what they do with everything else
suites.why: A file that ends early is a NullPointerException and not a PicardException: the reader answers null and the matcher is handed it without a guard. A file of only a header and dashes writes a metrics file with no table at all, not even the column line. And the three patterns are strict where it matters and loose where it does not: the dashes are not counted, the columns split on runs of whitespace, and the fraction may open on a dot but may not be negative.

cases.why: Thirteen cases: one row and three, spaces instead of tabs, a single dash, a fraction opening on a dot, a positive likelihood, a negative fraction and a negative id, a short row, a wrong header, a file of only a header and dashes, a file of only a header, and an empty file.

suites.title: bafRegress' stdout parsed, and the one column the tool derives
suites.why: Three failures with three different classes: a header that is not the header is a PicardException quoting it in single quotes, a row with the wrong number of columns is an IOException counting the columns it found, and a fractional Nhom is a NumberFormatException that escapes the wrapper entirely. An empty file is a fourth, a NullPointerException on String.equals. LOG10_PVAL is derived and not read, so a p-value of zero gives an infinity the writer renders as `-?`.

cases.why: Thirteen cases: one row and three, spaces in the row and in the header, a wrong header, a zero p-value, a negative estimate, exponent notation, a fractional Nhom, a short row and a long one, a file of only a header, and an empty file.

suites.title: which base reaches the depth histogram and which counter takes the rest
suites.why: The seven exclusion counters are a partition of the bases that did not count, and the fixture puts one base in each. GENOME_TERRITORY is the NON-N bases of the reference and not the covered ones, so it is 190 of 200. A wholly overlapping pair covers its span at depth ONE, the second end's bases going to PCT_EXC_OVERLAP. An N base is excluded by QUALITY whatever its quality says. And --INCLUDE_BQ_HISTOGRAM adds a third COLUMN rather than a second table.

cases.why: Thirteen cases: an unpaired read counted and not, a disjoint pair and a wholly overlapping one, a read under the mapping-quality floor, one half under the base-quality floor, one with N bases, a duplicate, a pair with one end unmapped, ten reads capped and not, the histogram, and a file with no reads.

suites.title: CollectWgsMetrics with four defaults changed, and what those four change
suites.why: The tool is CollectWgsMetrics with four defaults changed and nothing else, so the same fixture goes through both and the difference between the two files is the difference between the two sets of defaults. The mapping-quality floor is ZERO, so a read at quality five is counted here and excluded whole there; the base-quality floor is THREE, which the pair of cases at quality two and quality five straddles; and an N base is still excluded, quality zero being under three as it is under twenty. The histogram is trimmed past its last non-zero bin: the cap of a hundred thousand writes a hundred thousand and one bins, and keeping them cost two and a half megabytes and the slowest shard in CI.

cases.why: Eleven cases: a read under the other tool's mapping-quality floor, bases at quality two and five, N bases, an unpaired read counted and not, a duplicate, an overlapping pair and a disjoint one, ten reads, and a file with no reads. Only the `default-coverage-cap` case leaves the cap alone: the reference writes one histogram line per bin, and a hundred thousand of them per case was most of what this suite cost to run.

suites.title: how many distinct UMIs each duplicate set holds, and which reads reach a set
suites.why: The barcode-quality filter is INVERTED: `BarcodeQualityFilter.filterOut` returns `!badQuality`, so it drops the reads whose barcode is entirely above the floor and keeps the ones with a base under it. A file of well-formed barcodes reports nothing at all, and lowering the floor makes the tool report less rather than more. Every read of the fixture carries one bad barcode base so the other nine behaviours can be seen past it.

cases.why: Sixteen cases: three sets of one UMI, one set of three and one of two, a read with no UMI tag, the barcode-quality filter three ways, an unaligned read, one under the mapping-quality floor, a secondary one, an unpaired read filtered and kept, the tags named by argument, a lowered barcode floor, every read filtered, and no reads at all.

suites.title: two artifact tables rewritten as the older OxoG one, which is arithmetic and no reads
suites.why: The conversion is not a copy: an output row for `ACA` takes its pre-adapter figures from the input's `TGT`, the reverse complement, while its bait-bias figures come from `ACA` itself, so one output row draws on two different input rows. The two floors differ: the oxidation rate is floored at ONE BASE and the two bait-bias rates at 1e-10, which reads as a Q of exactly 100. The rows come out of two HashSets, so the dump sorts them: the order is a hash and not a behaviour.

cases.why: Eight cases: one context, the oxidation floor, the bait-bias floor and its reverse, two libraries by two contexts, an output basename, the file named outright, and neither named at all.

suites.title: the connected components of a crosscheck table, and which rows come back inside them
suites.why: The output carries every comparison whose BOTH sides are in one cluster whatever its own LOD, so a row at -5 comes back inside the cluster its neighbours built. A group in no edge at all reaches no cluster and its comparisons vanish entirely rather than forming a cluster of one. And the cluster identifier is a node INDEX and not a counter, so two clusters of two are numbered 0 and 2. The order of the output is a hash order, which is why the dump sorts before emitting.

cases.why: Twelve cases: a transitive chain, a threshold that splits it, a LOD exactly at the threshold and just above, two clusters, an orphan group, a self-comparison, a duplicated row, the default threshold, nothing above the threshold, and an empty file.

suites.title: the contaminating sample's genotype likelihoods at the haplotype map's sites
suites.why: A read is evidence for one haplotype BLOCK and not for every site it overlaps, which is why the fixture gives each block its own reads. The block's minor-allele frequency is the prior, so the same pileup at a middling quality reports 0,13,30 where the frequency is 0.4 and 0,12,30 where it is 0.3. --EXTRACT_CONTAMINATION is FALSE by default and flips the argument rather than the output, so a default run given 0.5 is asking about the contaminated sample. And --LOCUS_MAX_READS bounds the block rather than the record: forty reads under a cap of ten give a depth of sixteen at the block of two SNPs.

cases.why: Fifteen cases: the major and minor pileups at half contamination, contamination of nought and one, --EXTRACT_CONTAMINATION twice, another tool's argument named here, a base matching neither allele, two base qualities, a deep pileup capped and not, a sample alias, every SNP rather than the representatives, no reads, and two samples in one file.

suites.title: ExtractFingerprint with one argument negated, and what that negation changes
suites.why: The tool is ExtractFingerprint with EXTRACT_CONTAMINATION set from the negation of its own EXTRACT_CONTAMINATED, so its DEFAULT is the other tool's opposite: it reports the contaminant and names the sample `-contaminant`. At a contamination of 0.5 the flip is numerically a no-op and only the name tells the two apart; at nought and one the PLs are each other's. LOCUS_MAX_READS defaults to two hundred rather than fifty.

cases.why: Eleven cases: the major and minor pileups by default, the other tool's default restored, contamination of nought and one, a hundred reads capped and not, a sample alias, a base matching neither allele, no reads, and two samples in one file.

suites.title: the zCall genotype merged into a genotyping-array VCF, and what the tool swallows
suites.why: Every failure is SWALLOWED: doWork catches Exception, prints the stack trace and returns ZERO. There are two kinds. A failure before the writer opens leaves no file at all; one inside the record loop leaves a file holding its header and not one record, the writer having already opened it. The thresholds map is STATIC, so every run after the first holds every earlier run's thresholds and writes them onto records its own file never named. And a VCF whose genotypes carry nothing but GT cannot be processed, the map getExtendedAttributes answers being immutable when there are none.

cases.why: Nine cases in a fixed order, the last depending on it: agreeing and disagreeing PEDs, thresholds for one SNP, for all three and as NA, one NA of a pair, an A allele that is the reference, an allele of two characters, a two-sample VCF, a VCF of nothing but GT, and the static map's leak.

suites.title: several metrics tables merged into one, and what the round trip loses
suites.why: The merge is LOSSY and one input is enough to show it: the ratios are reconstructed from the printed columns by invertFromRatio, which rounds, and recomputed afterwards, so a single file of 301 SNPs at a TI/TV of 2.0 comes back at 2.01 having been merged with nothing at all. A ratio of NaN reconstructs as nought and comes back as nought. And the summary's reference bias is reconstructed against the DETAIL file beside it, the total het depth being summed over that file's detail rows.

cases.why: Nine cases: a round trip that divides evenly and one that does not, two inputs of one sample, two inputs of two samples, one input naming two samples, a NaN ratio, a summary of two rows, and a prefix whose files are not there.

suites.title: which variants are counted where, and what the derived columns make of the counts
suites.why: The known and the novel variants are counted apart in every column, and the fixture is built so the two TI/TV ratios differ rather than coinciding: 2 against 0.5. The summary is NOT the detail rows' sum, a two-sample file where one sample is hom-ref at half the sites reporting four SNPs in the summary, four for the first sample and two for the second. And an empty VCF still writes both files, PCT_DBSNP coming out `?` while the TI/TV columns come out `0`.

cases.why: Ten cases: known and novel mixed, nothing known, everything known, a filtered variant, indels, a multiallelic SNP, two samples, a target interval list, and an empty VCF.

suites.title: the same traversal reported twice, once over the whole territory and once over the covered part
suites.why: The tool is CollectWgsMetrics with a second row, and the second row is a recomputation over the same counts with the depth-zero bin dropped rather than a second traversal. A fully covered reference therefore makes the two rows identical, an uncovered half halves the second row's territory, and a file whose reads are all excluded divides by nought.

cases.why: Eleven cases: a pair covering part of the reference, reads covering all of it, an unpaired read excluded and counted, no reads at all, ten pairs uncapped and capped, the base-quality histogram, every read a duplicate, and the chart argument left out.

suites.title: which read reaches which of the eight oxidation counters, and what the rates make of them
suites.why: The counters turn on which END of the pair carries the alternate and on which strand it was read, which is the whole of the 8-oxo-G argument: `G>T` in read one and `C>A` in read two are the oxidised state, and the same substitutions in the other end are the control. The row order is a HashMap's over the context strings, so it reaches the file unsorted, and a G site is folded into the reverse complement of its context rather than getting a row of its own.

cases.why: Twenty-two cases: the reference alone, the alternate at a G site in each end and on each strand, at a C site in each end, the base-quality floor, the OQ tag honoured and ignored, the mapping-quality floor, both ends of the insert-size window, a duplicate, a secondary alignment, the first base of the contig, context size zero, a restricted context set, two contexts the validation refuses, two libraries, the debugging stop, a known site, an interval list, and a file with no read group.

suites.title: which read reaches which artifact counter, and what the five files carry
suites.why: A pre-adapter artifact is one whose direction follows the READ and a bait-bias one is one whose direction follows the REFERENCE STRAND, which is what the same substitution in read one and in read two tells apart. The output argument is a prefix for five files, the detail ones holding a row per substitution per context, and the summary ones the worst context per substitution. --CONTEXTS_TO_PRINT cuts the detail files and the error summary and not the counting: the twelve summary rows are the same whether it is given or not. --TANDEM_READS swaps read two's half of every sum, which is invisible on a pair whose ends are on opposite strands and plain on a substitution carried by read two on the forward strand: PRO_ALT and CON_ALT trade places and the Q goes from a hundred to eleven.

cases.why: Twenty-two cases: a clean pair, the same substitution in each end and on each strand, tandem reads on a pair whose ends are on opposite strands and on one carried by read two on the forward strand, context size nought, a restricted context set, a file extension, the base-quality floor with the OQ tag honoured and ignored, and each whole-read filter with the three that can be turned off shown both ways.

suites.title: a hybrid-selection experiment counted against its baits and its targets
suites.why: The baits and the targets are counted separately and a read may be on one and not the other: the same file reports sixty on-bait bases and a hundred on-target ones, because one target lies outside every bait. --NEAR_DISTANCE moves the window the middle column counts, and at nought its hundred and twenty bases become off-bait ones. CLIP_OVERLAPPING_READS is already true here: the shared argument defaults to false and this tool's own constructor sets it, which is why passing `true` changes nothing and passing `false` takes the on-target bases from a hundred to a hundred and twenty.

cases.why: Fourteen cases: a plain run, the per-target and per-base files, a near distance of nought, a named bait set, a mapping-quality floor above every read and a base-quality floor above every base, the clipping argument turned on and off, an overlapping pair three ways, a file with no reads, and a pair at mapping quality nought.

suites.title: the same collector under the amplicon column names
suites.why: The tool is CollectHsMetrics' collector with the baits called amplicons, so what the golden is for is the column names and the places the two tools do NOT agree. The arithmetic is the same: the three amplicon columns partition the aligned bases as the bait ones do, and the same fixture answers the same numbers under the other names.

cases.why: Eleven cases: a plain run, the per-target and per-base files, a near distance of nought, a named amplicon set, a mapping-quality floor above every read and a base-quality floor above every base, an overlapping pair with and without clipping, no reads at all, and a pair at mapping quality nought.

suites.title: which pairs a group calls duplicates, and the estimate the histogram gives
suites.why: The grouping is on the first MIN_IDENTICAL_BASES of BOTH ends and the comparison then SKIPS that prefix, so a difference inside it is not an error: it is what put two pairs in different groups. The rate is over both reads' compared length and floored, and the quality floor is an integer division, so a mean of 19.9 is dropped at twenty. A bin holding fewer than MIN_GROUP_COUNT groups is dropped from the metrics and kept in the histogram, the default being two, and an optical duplicate is subtracted before the Lander-Waterman estimate runs.

cases.why: Nineteen cases: two and three identical pairs, a difference at the sixth base under two seeds, a difference inside the seed, two diff rates, a low mean quality with the floor at its default and lowered, an N in the seed, a read shorter than the seed, the group-count floor both ways, two duplicate groups, a fixture deep enough to estimate from, two optical duplicates, two libraries, no duplicate at all, and a difference on each side of --MAX_READ_LENGTH.

suites.title: which pair of genotype states a site is filed under, and the three files it reaches
suites.why: A low quality, a low depth, a filter and a missing site are STATES here and not exclusions: the site is still counted, under another name, which is why --MIN_GQ moves a row rather than dropping one. The three files are one basename's, and the contingency table is the same data as four counters a state pair may contribute to more than once.

cases.why: Twelve cases: a plain run, every row kept, the two floors, filters ignored, a missing site read as missing, the hom-ref flag refused without an interval list and accepted with one, an interval list on its own, a no-call, and a second sample named out of a two-sample file.

suites.title: which programs one pass runs, and which files they land on
suites.why: The tool is a dispatcher and not an arithmetic: it builds one instance per PROGRAM and hands every one of them the same records. The default set is five of the eight programs the enum declares, an extension lands on the metrics file and not on the chart, and the charts are R's output, which two runs of one fixture do not agree on byte for byte.

cases.why: Eighteen cases: the default set and the same set twice over, a set named by the run, an empty set, an extension, the two programs that need a reference and the one that needs a refflat, an argument reaching one program, an argument for a program that is not running, a malformed one, an unknown program, an argument the pass owns, a truncated pass, a second accumulation level, and the same fixture through one program on its own.

suites.title: which cytosines an RRBS run counts, and which of them are CpG
suites.why: A CpG is looked for in the REFERENCE and not in the read, so a read that reads TG over a reference CG is a converted site rather than a mismatch. The rules around that do not compose the way the code reads: the last base of a block is never a CpG, the two quality thresholds are different numbers, and the non-CpG branch reads its quality off the whole read with the block's own index where the CpG branch reads the block's.

cases.why: Twenty-three cases: an unconverted read and a converted one, a CpG at and one before the last base, the two quality thresholds on each side, a negative strand, a soft-clipped read where the two quality readings diverge, the length and mismatch filters with the rounding boundary, a read with no CpG, the sequence filter on both sides, a second accumulation level, a prefix with and without its dot, a queryname-sorted file on both paths, and an empty file.

suites.title: which duplicate sets count as independent replicates, and what takes a site out
suites.why: A duplicate set whose reads disagree on the allele at a heterozygous site cannot have come from one molecule, which is the whole estimate. The filters around that sit at four different levels: the SITE (its genotype and its quality), the READ (its mapping quality and its pairing), the BASE (its quality) and the BARCODE (its own quality), and only the first is a property of the VCF.

cases.why: Twenty-two cases: a doubleton that disagrees and two that agree, one that shares a UMI, a tripleton, a set of four, a third allele, a homozygous and a low-quality site on both sides of the floor, a low mapping quality, a low base quality on both sides, unpaired reads on both sides, a low-quality barcode, another barcode tag, the optional matrix file, the three sample rules, and a stop after one set.

suites.title: what an array's calling metrics take from the VCF header and what they take from its variants
suites.why: Almost everything the tool reports comes out of the VCF's HEADER and not out of its variants: the chip, the sample, the two genders, the call rate the genotyping software reported, the dates, the cluster file and the twenty-three control codes. Which of those header lines are required and which are optional is not guessable, and a missing one is a refusal naming the line.

cases.why: Eighteen cases: a plain run and one whose dbSNP knows nothing, a filtered assay and the two filters that are not the same fate, the GTA attribute on both sides, an indel, seven headers each missing one line, the call-rate threshold on each side, and two processors against one.

suites.title: the lockstep an array VCF merge walks in, and everything it refuses
suites.why: The merge is not by position: the nth variant of each file is merged with the nth of every other, so two files holding the same loci in a different order are a refusal rather than a reordering. Seven attributes are exempt from the agreement check, DP is summed rather than compared, and the sample-specific header lines are dropped from the merged header.

cases.why: Sixteen cases: two, three and one sample, a repeated sample, the same loci in another order, a different count, locus, id, reference allele, alternate allele and alternate count, an attribute present in one file only, one that disagrees, an exempt one that disagrees, two depths that are summed, and two filters that are unioned.

suites.title: Maq's binary fastq: one byte per base, and which reads reach it
suites.why: One byte carries the base in its top two bits and the quality in its bottom six, so the file is byte-comparable and the questions are which reads reach it and what each byte says. An N is written as an A whose quality is not the read's, and clipping an adapter rewrites the tail rather than shortening the record.

cases.why: Nineteen cases: a pair, every base in both cases, an N inside and outside the seed region, an unknown base, a low quality, two pairs plain, chunked and truncated, a single-end run, the two length arguments, a vendor-failed read on both sides, the name prefix matching and not, and the two ways of naming the output given apart and together.

suites.title: the adpc.bin an array VCF becomes, field by field
suites.why: A record is twenty bytes, little-endian and uncompressed, so the file is byte-comparable. The genotype in it is an ILLUMINA one decided by the ALLELE_A and ALLELE_B header fields rather than by the reference and alternate alleles, and an allele that is the reference carries a trailing star those fields are stripped of before matching.

cases.why: Fourteen cases: the three called genotypes and the no-call, the allele fields reversed and one carrying a star, an intensity at and over the limit of an unsigned short, a missing normalized intensity, two loci, two samples, two VCFs agreeing and disagreeing on their length, and a VCF with no records.

suites.title: where an adapter starts, as the XT tag counts it
suites.why: The tool marks rather than clips: the XT tag is the ONE-BASED position the adapter starts at, found by a search that runs from the end of the read towards its front and takes the last start that matches. The error allowance is truncated from the OVERLAP's length rather than the adapter's, so a match near the end of a read allows fewer mismatches than one further in.

cases.why: Fifteen cases: an adapter at the first base and one halfway, no adapter, eleven and twelve bases of it with the minimum moved, one and two mismatches with the rate moved, a pair whose reads agree and one whose reads do not, a single named adapter, a custom pair, and a read that already carries a tag with and without an adapter.

suites.title: whether a file's sample is the sample its genotypes claim, and by how much
suites.why: The answer is a LOD score per haplotype block, positive for agreement and negative for disagreement, and the fixture is the extractfingerprint suite's own: three sites, two of them in one block, so a file that covers one block is fewer rows and not a row of zeros. A sample the genotypes do not carry is a RETURN CODE and not an exception.

cases.why: Eleven cases: reads agreeing and disagreeing with the genotypes, heterozygous and homozygous-alternate calls, a one-read pileup, a file covering one block, no reads at all, a sample the genotypes do not have with and without the expected alias, and a two-sample genotype file with each of the two named.

suites.title: which record of a duplicate set keeps the bit clear, and what the metrics count
suites.why: Duplicates are decided by the 5' position and the orientation and not by the bases, so soft clipping moves the position a read is compared at. Which record of a set keeps the bit clear is the scoring strategy's answer, and optical duplicates are a subset told apart by the tile coordinates in the read NAME rather than by anything in the alignment.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite, and identical to the local smoke run. 18 cases: the input and the marked output as SAM text plus the metrics table and its histogram, so what is compared is which record keeps 0x400 clear and what the counters say.

suites.title: the two mate-cigar duplicate markers, beside MarkDuplicates on the same inputs
suites.why: MarkDuplicates decides a pair's position from the two ends it has seen and so holds every unpaired end until its mate arrives. These two decide it from the MC tag instead, which makes one pass over a coordinate-sorted file enough and changes what they can see: a pair whose mate is soft-clipped is keyed on the mate's unclipped end. They also break ties differently from MarkDuplicates, which is why every case records all three tools' output.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite, and identical to the local smoke run. Eleven inputs through three tools: seven cases where all three agree, and four where the mate-cigar pair does not, each by name.

suites.title: the UMI-aware duplicate marker, and the second metrics table it writes
suites.why: A UMI is a barcode on the molecule rather than on the library, so two reads at one position carrying different UMIs are not duplicates of each other. This tool is SimpleMarkDuplicatesWithMateCigar with that split applied inside each duplicate set, and the split has a threshold: MAX_EDIT_DISTANCE_TO_JOIN is one by default, so two UMIs a single base apart are still one molecule.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite, and identical to the local smoke run. Eleven runs with the marked output, the duplication metrics and the UMI metrics table.

suites.title: every pair of fingerprints against every other, and the verdict on each
suites.why: CheckFingerprint asks whether one file's sample is the sample a set of genotypes says it is. This one asks the question of every PAIR of inputs with nothing to compare against but each other, so what is expected comes from the sample NAMES rather than from a set of genotypes: two read groups of one sample are expected to match, and a match between two samples is unexpected however good the LOD is.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that sorted the matrix's columns, and identical to the local smoke run. Thirteen runs, all four verdicts, three shapes of row and three exit codes.

suites.title: how good a fingerprint is on its own, and the deprecated crosscheck wrapper
suites.why: CalculateFingerprintMetrics asks how good a fingerprint is with nothing to compare it against: it samples the haplotype blocks and reports how far the observed genotypes are from what the panel's allele frequencies predict. CrosscheckReadGroupFingerprints is CrosscheckFingerprints with its defaults moved, deprecated in the reference, and it REFUSES combinations its parent accepts, which is behaviour a port has to reproduce rather than inherit.

cases.why: Eleven runs: six of CalculateFingerprintMetrics over one and two read groups, the three CALCULATE_BY values, two samples and the other allele; and five of CrosscheckReadGroupFingerprints, its two roll-ups and its two refusals. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: how often a base disagrees with the reference, and everything the tool refuses to count
suites.why: The empirical quality is Bayesian rather than a ratio: PRIOR_Q is a pseudo-count in phred space, so a file with no errors reports a finite number. What makes the tool more than a mismatch counter is what it declines to count: a site the VCF says the sample is polymorphic at, a base below a quality, a read below a mapping quality, and the second observation of a pair that overlaps itself.

cases.why: Fifteen runs: two mismatches and none, the prior moved, three stratifiers, two metrics in one run, a known site, the two thresholds each side of their cut, an overlapping pair, a deletion, a cap on the loci, and the collection argument that is appended to rather than replaced. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: whether a basecalls directory has the files a run would need
suites.why: Picard's Illumina tools read a DIRECTORY rather than a file, and the reference's own test data is not in the pinned clone, so the fixture is written byte by byte from the formats the readers document. This is the cheapest of those tools and the one that says what the others will refuse: which files are missing, for which tile and which cycle, and what the read structure asks for.

cases.why: Twelve runs over a four-cycle, one-tile, four-cluster run directory written byte by byte: complete, a cycle removed and the same one not asked for, more cycles than there are, the filter removed, the per-tile positions removed (which the default data types do not ask for), the lane's `s.locs` removed with and without the positions asked for, a tile that is there and one that is not, and the argument that writes what is missing instead of refusing. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: what a lane's tile metrics say, and what the tool does with a file that is missing half of them
suites.why: The tool reads one binary file and nothing else: the metrics come off the METRIC CODES in InterOp/TileMetricsOut.bin rather than off any basecall. 100 is the cluster count, 101 the count that passed the filter, 102 and 103 their densities, and a file carrying only some of them reports the rest as zero rather than refusing.

cases.why: Nine runs over tile metrics files written record by record: one tile, two tiles summed into a lane, two lanes as two rows, counts without densities and densities without counts, a code nobody reads, a named output prefix, no read structure at all, and a longer one. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: which declared barcode a cluster is, and when it is none of them
suites.why: The match is by edit distance rather than equality, and it is TWO tests: a cluster within MAX_MISMATCHES of a declared barcode is that barcode only if the next best is further away by MIN_MISMATCH_DELTA, so two barcodes a single base apart leave every cluster unmatched. A cluster that matches nothing is still written, and the metrics count the clusters that passed the filter apart from the rest.

cases.why: Eleven runs over the shared four-cluster fixture read as `2T2B`: two barcodes, one, one nobody carries, a barcode one base away with the mismatch allowance each side of its cut, two EQUIDISTANT barcodes with and without a delta, a quality floor below and above the fixture's bases, a barcode of the wrong length (which crashes rather than refusing), and the argument that names barcodes without a file. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: the FASTQ a basecalls directory becomes, and what the read structure leaves out of it
suites.why: This is the tool the Illumina family exists for. The read structure cuts the same cycles into different reads, and a barcode or a skip segment is not written at all, so four cycles are one read of four bases or two of two or one of two. The read name carries the run, the lane, the tile and the cluster's coordinates, which is where the .locs floats end up, and MULTIPLEX_PARAMS splits the output by the barcode ExtractIlluminaBarcodes would have found.

cases.why: Ten runs over the shared four-cluster fixture: the cycles as one read, as two, with a barcode segment and with a skip; the filtered cluster in and out; the two read name formats; and four multiplexed runs, including a barcode the params do not declare with and without the argument that ignores it. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: a lane's clusters counted per barcode
suites.why: The summary a run gets once ExtractIlluminaBarcodes has decided which barcode each cluster is: the counts are per barcode with a row for the clusters that matched none, the PF columns come from the filter file rather than from the basecalls, and the read structure decides how many cycles count as bases at all.

cases.why: Five runs over the shared four-cluster fixture: the whole lane as one row, the lane split by barcode after an extraction, a barcode segment with no barcodes given, a skipped segment, and a lane the run does not have. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: the unaligned BAM a basecalls directory becomes
suites.why: The same walk as IlluminaBasecallsToFastq with a different destination, and the difference is what a BAM can say that a FASTQ cannot: two template reads become a PAIR with the flags to prove it, the filter file becomes the vendor-check flag on a record that is still there rather than a record that is gone, the barcode becomes a tag, and the run's identity is written once in a read group instead of into every read name.

cases.why: Nine runs over the shared four-cluster fixture: one record a cluster and two that are a pair, a barcode segment and a skip, the failing cluster flagged and then dropped, the barcode in the read group's identifier, and three multiplexed runs including a barcode the params do not declare with and without the argument that ignores it. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: why a cluster failed the filter, classified per tile
suites.why: The filter file says a cluster failed; this tool says why, by looking at the first cycles of the read. A cluster whose bases are missing is one kind of failure, one whose bases are poor is another, and one that looks fine is a third, so the classes are a partition of the count the filter file gives rather than an independent measurement.

cases.why: Five runs over the shared four-cluster fixture: the lane as it is, two cycles to judge by, more cycles than the run carries, the sampled second file, and a lane the run does not have. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: the bytes a buffer passes through, and the shape it refuses
suites.why: The smallest tool in Picard: it copies its input to its output through a CIRCULAR buffer so a pipeline can decouple a slow writer from a slow reader. What there is to measure is that the bytes come out unchanged whatever the buffer's shape, including the bytes a text tool would mangle, and what it does when the shape is impossible.

cases.why: Eight runs: a line of text, nothing at all, a buffer smaller than the input and one of a single byte, an IO size above the buffer, six bytes that are not text, and a hundred thousand bytes through the default buffer and through a small one. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: a variant moved to another reference, and the three ways that fails
suites.why: Moving a variant through a chain file is arithmetic; what makes the tool interesting is what happens when the target reference disagrees with the source. A variant outside every block, one whose reference allele the target does not carry, and one on a reversed block are three different answers, and the reject file carries a filter naming which.

cases.why: Ten runs over a chain with one forward block offset by twelve and one reversed block: a variant inside a block, between the blocks, inside the reversed one, a reference mismatch with no recovery available, a swapped reference and alternate with and without the argument that recovers it, the two arguments that record where a variant came from, and three variants at once to see the order the output is written in. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: a trio's impossible genotypes, and the calls the checker declines to look at
suites.why: A child's alleles come one from each parent, so a call that cannot be explained that way is a violation. What makes the tool more than that arithmetic is everything it declines to count: a call below a genotype quality or a depth, a heterozygous call whose allele depths do not look heterozygous, a contig on the skip list, and the sex chromosomes, where a male child's X is haploid and a het call is its own kind of violation.

cases.why: Twelve runs over a trio VCF written record by record: a possible child, two violations counted to different parents, a low-quality call with the floor each side of it, a shallow call, a lopsided heterozygote, the X for a male and a female child, the mitochondrion, a run that asks for the offending records to be written (which the reference refuses with a duplicate-sample-name error), and a tab report. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: the baits a target list becomes, and what happens to a target too small to tile
suites.why: The tool lays fixed-length probes along each target, and the answer is decided by the strategy, the bait's size and offset, and what it does with a target shorter than a bait: it still gets MINIMUM_BAITS_PER_TARGET of them, which means baits running off both ends. The four strategies lay the same target four different ways, which is what makes the argument worth measuring rather than describing.

cases.why: Eleven runs over a synthetic reference: a target longer than a bait and one shorter, the minimum lowered, the three strategies, a smaller bait, a wider offset, padding, and two nearby targets merged and unmerged. The parameters file is skipped: it is the tool's own usage text rather than anything the design decided. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: Illumina's binary bead pool manifest, read and written out as a normalization CSV
suites.why: The genotyping-array tools read Illumina's binary manifests, and the reference's own test data is not in the pinned clone, so the fixture is written byte by byte from the format the parser documents by reading it. This is the smallest of those tools and the one that says whether a manifest parses at all: the normalization id it reports is not the one in the file but that id plus a hundred times the assay type, and the two fields the parser cross-checks are refused by name when they disagree.

cases.why: Six runs over manifests written record by record: four loci of two assay types, one locus of each type alone, an assay type disagreeing with its B address each way round, and a normalization id above the hundred the parser allows. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: two genotype call files compared field by field
suites.why: A GTC is not a stream but a TABLE OF CONTENTS: an id and an absolute offset per kind of data, and the reader seeks. The fixture writer lays the payloads out and writes the table over the top, which is what makes measuring this family possible at all. The tool compares every getter by reflection, so what it reports names Java methods, and the fields expected to differ between two runs of one chip are excluded by name rather than compared and forgiven.

cases.why: Seven runs over GTC files written record by record: two identical files, a different sample name (which is excluded from the comparison rather than reported), one and two different genotypes, different intensities, a different call rate, and a file with one locus fewer. What is recorded is the STATUS: the differences themselves go through log4j, which holds the stream it was initialised with, so an in-process dump cannot capture them. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: a chip's genotype calls turned into a VCF
suites.why: The tool reads four files to write one: the calls, the bead pool manifest that says what a locus is, the cluster file that says how the call was made, and the extended manifest that says where the locus sits on the target build and which alleles it has there. The genotype is written against the BUILD's alleles rather than the chip's A and B, and a no-call is written rather than dropped.

cases.why: Six runs over fixtures written record by record: four loci on two contigs called AA, AB, BB and no-call, one of which comes out TRIALLELIC because the build's reference base is neither of the chip's alleles; every call homozygous reference; every call a no-call; a locus flagged ILLUMINA_FLAGGED and one flagged DUPE, each of which is dropped rather than filtered; and a sample the command line declares male. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

suites.title: the extended manifest GtcToVcf reads, and the loci it flags rather than drops
suites.why: The tool works out, per locus, where it sits on the target build and which alleles it has there, which is the file GtcToVcf reads. The answer is not a copy of the input: a locus whose position is not on the build is FLAGGED rather than dropped, and the flag is what the downstream tool acts on, so the two suites meet at that column.

cases.why: Four runs over manifests written record by record: four loci the reference carries, the same with an empty dbSNP, a locus on a contig the reference does not have, and a locus past the end of its contig. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added it, and identical to the local smoke run.

probes.title: Decision 0020 (htsjdk-rs): is CollectRnaSeqMetrics order-independent?
probes.on_failure: CollectRnaSeqMetrics is no longer order-independent. htsjdk-rs decision 0020 must be revisited.
probes.why: OverlapDetector in htsjdk-rs skips a byte-exact IntervalTree because the overlap set is folded commutatively by this Picard tool. The probe belongs here, not in htsjdk-rs, because it instantiates CollectRnaSeqMetrics and only the Picard oracle has it. Two runs differ iff the HashSet<Gene> order reaches the output; identical means it does not.
